A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CARE Transformer work and are readable throughout, including equations, figures, tables and references. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification, detection and segmentation experiments, mobile latency measurements, and component ablations in Tables 1–5.

after.justification: V2 retains the original benchmark results, latency measurements and ablations in Tables 1–5.

M1.justification: Sections 3.3–3.5 retain the asymmetrical channel split, dynamic memory, dual interaction module and CARE-S0/S1/S2 architectures. Added explanatory wording does not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ImageNet-1K classification, COCO object detection and instance segmentation, and ADE20K semantic segmentation. The added image-editing references do not introduce an evaluated task.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1–2 is unchanged, including MLLA-T, FastViT-SA12 and MobileViGv2-M. The newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 and the table captions retain the same training budgets, optimizers, batch sizes, task heads, input resolutions, hardware and latency measurement settings.

E4.justification: Tables 3–5 retain the same decoupling comparisons, interaction and memory ablations, and early-convolution and multiscale analyses. No additional robustness or sensitivity analysis appears.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical results and findings in Figure 1 and Tables 1–5 are unchanged. Table 1 retains 78.4/80.1/82.1% ImageNet accuracy for CARE-S0/S1/S2; Table 2 retains CARE-S2's 43.1 box AP and 43.5 mIoU.

T1.justification: Equations 1–13, Propositions 1–3 and Proof 1 retain the same mathematical content and assumptions. Differences concern typesetting and placement.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about asymmetrical decoupling, complementary feature interaction, and the accuracy–efficiency balance of mobile models.

C2.justification: The added accuracy clause in Section 3.4 reiterates the existing feature-complementarity rationale. Experimental interpretations and the limitations concerning architecture search and larger models remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces v1's generic github link, which targets a local placeholder, with a specific CARE-Transformer repository address. Implementation details are unchanged, and both versions still describe code release in the future tense.

R1.justification: V2 adds five references, numbered 14 and 63–66, concerning multimodal generalists, partial multi-view learning, few-shot segmentation and drag-based editing. These extend the background and feature-complementarity discussion without changing the central positioning relative to MLLA.

P1.justification: Small wording additions appear in the introduction and Section 3.4, and the abstract displays the full repository address. Section order and nearly all explanatory prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is displayed slightly smaller, and spacing and text reflow alter equation, paragraph and bibliography placement. All three figures and five tables retain their content and overall organization.

improvement.justification: The specific repository address makes the intended code location identifiable, replacing v1's placeholder and providing a limited documentation improvement. Other changes concern citations, wording and layout; the scientific evidence is unchanged, and neither PDF establishes that code has been released.
